## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

The *Pāyasadāyakattheraapadāna* is a verse text belonging to the *Therāpadāna* within the Pali Khuddaka Nikāya [SuttaCentral]. The title indicates that it recounts the biographical and karmic narrative (*apadāna*) of the elder (*thera*) Pāyasadāyaka ("giver of milk-rice"). SuttaCentral lists five modern translations of the text in five languages [SuttaCentral].

No independent parallels are curated by SuttaCentral, but automated text-reuse analysis by DharmaNexus records 44 matching passages across 13 Pali texts [SuttaCentral; DharmaNexus]. The most substantial reuse occurs in the *Theragāthā-aṭṭhakathā* (first part), where segments 0.3–8.4 correspond closely to commentary sections (§§1829_9–1845), reflecting commentary citation or inclusion of the verses [DharmaNexus]. The remaining internal reuse consists primarily of conventional stock verses found in the closing portions of the poem (segments 7–11), which are shared with other *Therāpadāna* texts such as the *Kusumāsaniyattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 128), *Kilañjadāyakattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 236), *Sappidāyakattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 221), and *Bhikkhadāyakattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 103) [DharmaNexus]. DharmaNexus also detects slight cross-language alignments with the Tibetan *Suvarṇavarṇāvadāna* (D4144), though these machine matches possess low similarity scores and do not represent verified historical parallels [DharmaNexus].

*No discussion of this text was found in the reference-literature corpus; the overview relies on SuttaCentral and DharmaNexus data.*
